cohort: Neonates born in Emilia-Romagna, Italy, between 2009 and 2012
finding: While Group B Streptococcus (GBS) was the most common cause of early-onset sepsis (EOS), Escherichia coli was the leading cause of death and complications, particularly in preterm neonates.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was found to be significantly associated with death or brain lesions in neonates with early-onset sepsis.
